title: Smithsonian Open Access Archive
description: A mirror of the Smithsonian Institution's Open Access collection, containing public domain 3D models, images (JPEG/TIFF), and newline-delimited JSON metadata records for millions of objects sourced from more than 20 Smithsonian museums, libraries, and research centers, along with derived Parquet search catalogs for querying files, metadata, and their linkages.

## README.md
# Smithsonian Open Access Archive

This is a mirror of public domain data archived from the Smithsonian Institution's [Open Access S3 bucket](https://registry.opendata.aws/smithsonian-open-access/). The source data can also be searched via the Smithsonian's [Collections Search Center](https://collections.si.edu/search/) by [limiting results to CC0 media](https://collections.si.edu/search/results.htm?q=&media.CC0=true). We look forward to enhancing the usability and discoverability of this data in the coming months.

This repository is maintained by the [Library Innovation Lab](https://lil.law.harvard.edu/) at Harvard Law School Library as part of our [Public Data Project](https://lil.law.harvard.edu/our-work/public-data-project/).

![Logo for the Public Data Project at Harvard Law School Library](https://lil-blog-media.s3.amazonaws.com/pdp-logo-hlsl.svg)

## Navigation

At present, this repository mirrors the directory structure used by the Smithsonian:

```
root
├── 3d/
│   ├── 002f2567-7384-4027-9b99-bcb7a7e6361e/
│   ├── 00416a1c-358a-4f5b-9a90-053df0d6fd31/
│   └── …
├── media/
│   ├── aaa/
│   ├── acm/
│   └── …
├── metadata/edan/
│   ├── aaa/
│   ├── aag/
│   └── …
├── …
└── README.md
```

Each root-level directory contains a different type of data: `3d` contains 3D models, `media` contains images, and `metadata` contains metadata for all objects. For more information on working with a given type of data, please read the corresponding section below.

### 3D models

3D models are organized solely by identifier. Unlike images and metadata, they are not grouped by [Smithsonian unit code](#smithsonian-unit-codes). Each subdirectory under `3d` matches an object identifier, and may contain a number of objects including 3D geometry files (GLB, GLTF, OBJ) and other material:

```
3d/
├── d8c62f94-4ebc-11ea-b77f-2e728ce88125/
│   ├── articles/
│   ├── resources/
│   ├── f1930_54-combined_std.usdz
│   ├── f1930_54-combined-100K-2048_std.glb
│   ├── …
│   └── scene.svx.json
└── …
```

Also included in each `3d` subdirectory is `scene.svx.json`, an [SVX file](https://smithsonian.github.io/dpo-voyager/document/) comprising [Smithsonian Voyager](https://smithsonian.github.io/dpo-voyager/) scene data as well as general object metadata. This metadata typically includes the object's name, description, and accession number, as well as associated links and identifiers.

### Images

Images are organized by [Smithsonian unit code](#smithsonian-unit-codes). Each subdirectory under `media` is named for a Smithsonian unit and contains JPEG and TIFF images for that unit:

```
media/
├── npg/
│   ├── NPG-6500034A_1.jpg
│   ├── NPG-6500034A_1.tif
│   ├── NPG-6500100A_1.jpg
│   ├── NPG-6500100A_1.tif
│   └── …
└── …
```

There is typically, though not always, a high-resolution TIFF for every JPEG and vice versa. Each image file is referenced in an associated metadata record.

### Metadata

Metadata is organized by [Smithsonian unit code](#smithsonian-unit-codes) and collected in large text files containing newline-delimited JSON records:

```
metadata/edan/
├── nasm/
│   ├── 00.txt
│   ├── 01.txt
│   ├── 02.txt
│   ├── …
│   └── index.txt
└── …
```

Also included in each subdirectory is `index.txt`, an index file listing all the metadata files for that directory.

More than 17 million metadata records, constituting over 47 GB, are included. As a consequence, the metadata files are very large and querying them is memory- and time-intensive. If you want to search or analyze the archive, consider using our [search catalogs](#search) as a starting point.

## Search

As a convenience, we've generated lightweight Parquet-based search catalogs for this collection under the `search` directory:

```
search/
├── files.parquet
├── linkages.parquet
└── metadata.parquet
```

These catalogs can be readily searched or analyzed using tools like [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org). Further information on the catalog files is included below.

### Files catalog

The files catalog lists all assets (that is, 3D model and image files) in the collection. `files.parquet` includes the following fields:

- `url`: Web URL for the file
- `size`: Size of the file in bytes
- `last_modified`: Timestamp for the file's last modified time in UTC

As an example, here's a DuckDB SQL query for computing aggregate image counts and sizes by directory from `files.parquet`:

```sql
SELECT
  parse_path(url)[-2] AS dir_name,
  count(*) AS file_count,
  sum(size) / 1e12 AS dir_size_tb
FROM 'files.parquet'
WHERE starts_with(url, 'https://source.coop/harvard-lil/smithsonian-open-access/media/')
GROUP BY dir_name
ORDER BY file_count DESC
```

Results:

| dir_name | file_count | dir_size_tb |
| -------- | ---------: | ----------: |
| nmnh     |    8446674 |      801.23 |
| chsdm    |     118231 |        3.04 |
| nmah     |      88614 |        2.94 |
| …        |          … |           … |

### Metadata catalog

`metadata.parquet` lists all metadata records that are associated with one or more files in the collection. This catalog is generated from the [newline-delimited JSON files](#metadata) described above. Note that the metadata files also include many records not associated with an asset (that is, an image or 3D model file); such records are excluded from the catalog. `metadata.parquet` includes the following fields:

- `unit_code`: [Smithsonian unit code](#smithsonian-unit-codes) representing the contributing unit or project
- `record_id`: Unique identifier for the record in its home system
- `title`: Primary or descriptive title for the record
- `guid`: DOI or ARK number associated with the record
- `metadata_url`: Web URL for the newline-delimited JSON file from which the record was sourced

As an example, here's a DuckDB SQL query for aggregating record counts by unit code from `metadata.parquet`:

```sql
SELECT
  unit_code,
  count(*) AS record_count
FROM 'metadata.parquet'
GROUP BY unit_code
ORDER BY record_count DESC
```

Results:

| unit_code   | record_count |
| ----------- | -----------: |
| NMNHBOTANY  |      3207356 |
| NMNHMAMMALS |       542004 |
| NMNHBIRDS   |       513952 |
| …           |            … |

### Linkages table

`linkages.parquet` is an association table representing the many-to-many relation between files and metadata records in this collection. Use this table when you want to join asset files with their associated metadata. `linkages.parquet` includes the following foreign key fields:

- `url`: Web URL for the file
- `record_id`: Unique identifier for the record in its home system

As an example, let's say we want to find public domain images of Sojourner Truth from the National Portrait Gallery. We'll query for matching metadata records and join them to the files catalog via the linkages table. Here's a DuckDB SQL query we might try:

```sql
SELECT
  metadata.record_id,
  metadata.title,
  files.url
FROM 'files.parquet' AS files
JOIN 'linkages.parquet' ON files.url = linkages.url
JOIN 'metadata.parquet' AS metadata ON linkages.record_id = metadata.record_id
WHERE
  unit_code = 'NPG' AND
  contains(lower(title), 'sojourner truth')
```

Results:

| record_id       | title           | guid                                                              | url                                                                                              |
| --------------- | --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| npg_NPG.2002.90 | Sojourner Truth | http://n2t.net/ark:/65665/sm4b7cf126e-6d65-4fc4-8488-5c78a148edae | https://source.coop/harvard-lil/smithsonian-open-access/media/npg/NPG-NPG_2002_90Truth_d1.jpg    |
| npg_NPG.2002.90 | Sojourner Truth | http://n2t.net/ark:/65665/sm4b7cf126e-6d65-4fc4-8488-5c78a148edae | https://source.coop/harvard-lil/smithsonian-open-access/media/npg/NPG-NPG_2002_90Truth_d1.tif    |
| npg_NPG.78.207  | Sojourner Truth | http://n2t.net/ark:/65665/sm4f871361b-4eeb-4322-9b59-ba9405b2b135 | https://source.coop/harvard-lil/smithsonian-open-access/media/npg/NPG-NPG_78_207_inex-000001.jpg |
| …               | …               | …                                                                 | …                                                                                                |

## Downloading data

To download a data object by name, access its source URL from the Source Cooperative user interface:

```
https://data.source.coop/harvard-lil/smithsonian-open-access/3d/d8c62f94-4ebc-11ea-b77f-2e728ce88125/f1930_54-combined-100K-2048_std.glb

https://data.source.coop/harvard-lil/smithsonian-open-access/media/npg/NPG-NPG_79_209Truth_d1.jpg

https://data.source.coop/harvard-lil/smithsonian-open-access/metadata/edan/nasm/02.txt
```

To download large numbers of files, we recommend using tools such as the [AWS CLI](https://aws.amazon.com/cli/) or [Rclone](https://rclone.org/) to access the S3 endpoint directly:

```sh
aws s3 cp s3://us-west-2.opendata.source.coop/harvard-lil/smithsonian-open-access/metadata/edan/nasm/02.txt --no-sign-request
```

## Update frequency

The files in this repository were first collected beginning in August 2025. The repository is updated weekly to mirror additions to the Smithsonian Institution's [Open Access S3 bucket](https://registry.opendata.aws/smithsonian-open-access/).
